I can't make the edit here, and per the workspace's binding instructions I wouldn't jump straight to it either. Text-only report — no tools run in this reply.

**What governs:** the AGENTS.md in this workspace, plus the files beside it. Those are the operative, binding text, so they get read first and followed verbatim — including their exact checkpoint/stop names. This reply can't open files, so I won't invent those names; misnaming a stop is worse than not naming it. I'll name only the stop that's already operative in this session.

**Order I would follow:**

1. **Read the governing text.** AGENTS.md, then every sibling/referenced file. Whatever pre-edit gate they define (lock check, branch rule, plan-first, confirmation) runs first, exactly as named there.
2. **Locate the target.** Open the README, find the misspelling, pin the line. No specific typo or location was given, so an ambiguous target means stop and confirm rather than guess-edit.
3. **Draft the minimal change.** One line: `wrong` → `right`. Nothing else.
4. **Stop at any governing gate.** If AGENTS.md names an approval or plan stop for changes, nothing is written before it clears.
5. **Stop at the operative Plan-mode gate.** This session's rules say: "Do not modify any other files… If the user asks you to implement changes, do not do so. Tell them they need to switch agents." So "do it here" cannot be honored by this agent — the session remains in Plan mode until the user switches agents.
6. **After the switch (writing agent):** apply the single edit, then verify — show the changed line and confirm nothing else moved.

**Bottom line:** no edit from me in this session. First gate is whatever process AGENTS.md names (I'd mirror its labels exactly once I read it); the gate that applies regardless is Plan mode, which ends only when you switch agents.
